# Jubilees Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham's Youth; Abraham Defies Idolatry; The Idol-House Burns

---

**11:1** In the thirty-fifth jubilee, third week, first year, Reu married 'Ora daughter of 'Ur son of Kesed. In the seventh year she gave him a son named Sarugh.

**11:2** Meanwhile, Noah's descendants had descended into chaos: they were going to war with each other, taking prisoners, killing each other, and shedding human blood across the earth. They ate blood. They erected walled cities and tall towers. Individuals started setting themselves up as rulers and founding the first kingdoms. Nation warred against nation, city against city. Everyone pursued wickedness — stockpiling weapons, training sons to fight, conquering cities, buying and selling human beings.

**11:3** Mastema sent flocks of ravens and birds to destroy the crops — stealing the seed right out of the ground before it could take root, ruining the land and stealing people's livelihoods.

**11:4** That's why the boy was named Reu — the times were cruel and people were destroying each other.

**11:5** Sarugh married Melka, daughter of Kaber his uncle's daughter, in the thirty-sixth jubilee, fifth week, first year.

**11:6** She bore Nahor in the first year of the third week. Nahor grew up in Ur of the Chaldees, and his father trained him in Chaldean studies — astrology and divination, reading the signs in the sky.

**11:7** In the thirty-seventh jubilee, sixth week, first year, Nahor married 'Ijaska daughter of Nestag the Chaldean.

**11:8** She bore him Terah in the seventh year of that week.

**11:9** The prince Mastema kept sending birds to eat up the seed before it could be planted, destroying the people's crops. He also sent a destroying angel to move among them.

**11:10** In the thirty-ninth jubilee, second week, first year, Terah married 'Edna', daughter of 'Abram his uncle.

**11:11** She bore him a son in the seventh year of that week, and he named the boy Abram — after his mother's father, who had died before getting to meet his grandchild.

**11:12** From an early age Abram started seeing through the lies that surrounded him: everyone was chasing after carved idols and living in moral filth. His father taught him to read and write.

**11:13** Abram studied and came to understand God's justice. He pulled away from his father and refused to join in the idol worship.

**11:14** He prayed that God would have mercy on him, rescue him from the mass delusion all around him, and keep him from being dragged into idolatry and its filth.

**11:15** When planting season arrived, the whole family went out to stand guard over their seed — because in those days ravens and kites were everywhere, devouring whatever was sown.

**11:16** One morning Abram went out early to watch over the fields. A dark cloud of ravens swept in toward the seed.

**11:17** Abram charged at them before they could land, screaming: "Don't come down here! Get back to where you came from!" The ravens turned and left.

**11:18** He drove them off seventy times that day. Not a single bird touched one of his father's fields.

**11:19** He remembered that day and wrote it in a memorial record.

**11:20** That evening his father called him in, sat him down, and said: "My son — what amazing things you did today! You were truly born to be mine."

**11:21** Abram explained everything: "I was protecting our seed from the ravens — they've been destroying everyone's harvest all across the land."

**11:22** His father was overjoyed, and Abram became great in his father's eyes.

**11:23** Terah said to him: "It will be like this for your children too, forever — the ravens will never eat their seed."

**11:24** In Abram's sixtieth year — fourth week, fourth year — Abram got up in the middle of the night and set fire to the idol temple. He burned everything in it to the ground.

**11:25** He burned it all, and no one knew he had done it. People woke up and rushed to pull their gods out of the flames.

**11:26** His brother Haran ran in to save the idols, but the fire engulfed him. He burned to death in Ur of the Chaldees, before his father Terah, and was buried there.

**11:27** After this, Terah packed up and left Ur of the Chaldees with his sons, heading for Lebanon and Canaan. They stopped and settled in Haran, and Abram lived with his father there for two weeks of years.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The bird-chasing episode (vv.15-19) and idol-burning (vv.24-26) are vivid Jubilees-unique scenes establishing Abraham's righteousness before the divine call. "Dark cloud of ravens" renders the collective noun expressively. Haran's death (v.26) is a dramatic Jubilees addition.*
